AI application that creates clients and enforces consent (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, and similar hosts)
One connector inside the host; **1:1** with a single server
Process or remote service exposing tools / resources / prompts
Callable function the model may invoke (`tools/list`, `tools/call`)
Collective name for tools, resources, and prompts
Wire encoding for MCP requests, results, and errors
Local transport over stdin/stdout; one client per process
Remote transport: HTTP POST plus optional streaming response; no protocol session id
Older remote transport (GET SSE + POST); **Deprecated**; migrate to Streamable HTTP
No protocol-level sessions; no `initialize` handshake; each request is self-contained
Explicit opaque state token passed as ordinary tool arguments when cross-call state is needed
Required Streamable HTTP header naming the JSON-RPC method (e.g. `tools/call`)
Required Streamable HTTP header naming the tool/resource/prompt target when applicable
Mechanism to promote selected tool parameters into HTTP headers for gateway routing
Former stream resume mechanism; **removed**. Broken stream ⇒ re-issue with a **new** request id
**MUST**-implement RPC advertising supported protocol versions, capabilities, and identity
Per-request / per-result metadata bag (version, capabilities, clientInfo, serverInfo, …)
`_meta` key carrying the protocol version on every request
`_meta` key declaring what the client supports (elicitation, extensions, …)
`_meta` key; clients SHOULD identify name + version on each request
`_meta` key; servers SHOULD identify themselves on each result
Error when client and server protocol versions do not match (`-32022`)
Interface adding `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` on list/read results
Freshness hint in milliseconds for client-side caching of list/read results
`"public"` or `"private"`; whether shared intermediaries may cache the response
Servers SHOULD return tools in stable order for client and LLM prompt-cache hits
Field on ClientCapabilities / ServerCapabilities listing opt-in extensions
Multi Round-Trip Requests - pattern replacing server-initiated requests over a held-open stream ([SEP-2322](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/2322))
Result with `resultType: "input_required"` asking the client for more information before completion
Map of server-assigned ids → request objects (`elicitation/create`, `sampling/createMessage`, `roots/list`)
Map the client sends on retry; keys match `inputRequests`
Opaque server-owned blob echoed unchanged on retry; treat as attacker-controlled on the server
Server asks the user for structured input (via MRTR `elicitation/create`)
Server asks the host LLM to complete a message - feature **Deprecated**; still usable via MRTR during the window
Workspace root listing - feature **Deprecated**; still usable via MRTR during the window
Out-of-band browser/user flow; completion is learned by retrying the original request (no `notifications/elicitation/complete`)
Long-lived POST response stream for opt-in server-to-client change notifications
Subscription type for tool catalog changes
Subscription type for prompt catalog changes
Subscription type for resource catalog changes
Subscription type for specific resource update notifications
Tag on notifications acknowledging which listen subscription they belong to
e.g. `notifications/progress`, `notifications/message` on the **request** response stream, not `subscriptions/listen`
Former session log-level RPC; **removed** (use per-request `logLevel` in `_meta`)
Cancellation signal; on Streamable HTTP, closing the response stream is cancellation; this notification is stdio-oriented
Official extension `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` for durable async work ([SEP-2663](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/2663))
Client-to-server mid-flight input for a task
Former task listing RPC; **removed** from the redesigned extension
Server-returned reference a client uses with `tasks/get` / `update` / `cancel`; may be returned unsolicited
Extension letting servers deliver interactive HTML UIs hosts render in a sandboxed iframe
Enterprise Managed Authorization - extension path for org-managed auth
Protocol log messages to client - **Deprecated**; prefer stderr (stdio) or OpenTelemetry
Preferred client registration: client publishes metadata at a URL used as its `client_id`
OAuth Dynamic Client Registration - **Deprecated** in favor of Client ID Metadata Documents
Clients MUST validate a present `iss` in auth responses against the recorded issuer ([RFC 9207](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9207))
Client credentials MUST be keyed by issuer; MUST NOT reuse across authorization servers
DCR field clients must set appropriately to avoid OIDC redirect URI conflicts
Hints about tool behavior; treat as untrusted unless the server is trusted
Host-enforced user approval for data access and tool invocation
Spec-reserved error when HTTP MCP headers disagree with the body
Client lacked a capability the server needed
`-32000`-`-32019` implementation-defined; `-32020`-`-32099` reserved for the MCP spec
Allowed keyword set for tool `inputSchema` / `outputSchema` (loosened in this revision)
Schema references must resolve under documented rules and resource bounds

lessons.title: 0001 . What is MCP?
lessons.summary:
Without a shared protocol, every AI product ships custom plugins. MCP standardizes how hosts discover and call tools and how servers expose data, so one server can serve many hosts.

Model Context Protocol is an open JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol that lets LLM applications share context and tools with external systems. Inspiration comes from the Language Server Protocol: one integration model, many editors (here: many AI hosts).

What servers can offer. Resources: Data / context for user or model Prompts: Templated workflows Tools: Functions the model may execute

What clients may offer. Elicitation: Ask the user for more input Sampling / Roots / Logging: Deprecated — do not build new features on them

Utilities. Configuration, progress, cancellation, error reporting, caching hints (ttlMs), subscriptions for list/resource changes.

lessons.title: 0002 . Architecture: host, client, server
lessons.summary:
Isolation is the product feature. The host coordinates many MCP clients; each client has a dedicated link to one server. Servers stay easy to build and composable, and they never read the whole conversation.

Roles. Host: Creates clients, enforces permissions/consent, aggregates context for the LLM Client: 1:1 with a server; attaches version/capabilities on every request; manages subscriptions Server: Exposes focused capabilities; local (stdio) or remote (Streamable HTTP)

Layers. Data layer — JSON-RPC: discovery, primitives, notifications, MRTR Transport layer — stdio or Streamable HTTP (framing, auth)

Principles. Servers should be extremely easy to build; Servers should be highly composable; Servers must not read the whole conversation or peer into other servers; Features can be added progressively via capabilities / extensions.

lessons.title: 0003 . Primitives: tools, resources, prompts
lessons.summary:
A database MCP server might expose a schema as a resource, a few-shot query helper as a prompt, and run_query as a tool. Same server, three different shapes of context.

Tools. Discovered with tools/list, invoked with tools/call Each tool has name, optional title, description, inputSchema (JSON Schema) Results return a content array (text, images, resources, …) and may include structured output Servers SHOULD return tools in a deterministic order (client caching / prompt-cache hits) List results carry ttlMs and cacheScope

Resources. resources/list / resources/read (+ templates) Stable URIs for files, records, API payloads Change notifications via subscriptions/listen when opted in

Prompts. prompts/list / prompts/get Parameterized templates for user or model-facing workflows

Discovery pattern. Hosts that federate many servers should use progressive tool discovery rather than dumping every tool into the model context at once (client best practices). Optional server/discover */list for the primitives you care about Call / read / get as needed Optionally subscriptions/listen for toolsListChanged, resourcesListChanged, …

lessons.title: 0004 . Transports: stdio and Streamable HTTP
lessons.summary:
Pick the transport for where the server lives. Same-machine tools (Draw.io, local calendar) fit stdio. Internet-hosted APIs fit Streamable HTTP with OAuth or tokens.

stdio. Fleet example: [mcp_servers.drawio] via npx @drawio/mcp@1.5.0 (stdio only — never the hosted https://mcp.draw.io/mcp endpoint). Host spawns the server process Messages on stdin / stdout No network hop; strong fit for local secrets that never leave the machine Typically one client per process

Streamable HTTP. If a response stream breaks, the client MUST re-issue as a new request with a new id. Client POSTs JSON-RPC to the server Optional streaming on the response Auth: bearer tokens, API keys, custom headers; OAuth recommended for user data As of 2026-07-28: no Mcp-Session-Id; no SSE Last-Event-ID resumability

Deprecated transport. HTTP+SSE (legacy) is Deprecated under the feature lifecycle. Migrate to Streamable HTTP.

lessons.title: 0005 . Stateless discovery and `_meta`
lessons.summary:
Stateless MCP means list endpoints do not secretly vary by connection, and load balancers do not need sticky sessions for protocol correctness. State that must survive across calls becomes an explicit handle in tool arguments.

What was removed. Protocol-level sessions / Mcp-Session-Id initialize / notifications/initialized handshake

What replaced them. Every request includes _meta fields such as:

server/discover. Servers MUST implement it Returns supportedVersions, capabilities, identity (serverInfo in result _meta) Clients MAY call it first or probe for compatibility (including on stdio) Response is typically cacheable (ttlMs, cacheScope)

Subscriptions. Change notifications are opt-in via subscriptions/listen. Request-scoped progress/message notifications still ride the original request's response stream.

lessons.title: 0006 . MRTR and elicitation
lessons.summary:
MRTR is the big interaction change in 2026-07-28. Servers no longer fire freestanding requests at the client. They reply with resultType: "input_required", and the client retries the same logical operation with the answers attached.

Flow. Client sends tools/call (or resources/read / prompts/get) Server needs user/LLM/roots input → InputRequiredResult Client fulfills inputRequests, echoes opaque requestState Client retries with a new JSON-RPC id and inputResponses Server returns resultType: "complete"

Allowed on. tools/call: Yes resources/read: Yes prompts/get: Yes Everything else: MUST NOT

lessons.title: 0007 . Extensions: Tasks, Apps, Auth
lessons.summary:
Extensions are disabled by default and need explicit support on both sides. That keeps simple servers simple while letting product hosts add charts-in-chat or async job handles when both parties agree.

Negotiation. Client: clientCapabilities.extensions["io.modelcontextprotocol/…"] Server: capabilities.extensions in server/discover Graceful degradation when only one side supports an extension

Official highlights. Experimental extensions live under experimental-ext-* repos and need a Working/Interest Group. Tasks (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks): Durable async handles; poll tasks/get; mid-flight input tasks/update; moved out of core in 2026-07-28 MCP Apps: Interactive UI (charts, forms, players) inside the host conversation OAuth client credentials: Machine-to-machine auth Enterprise-managed authorization: Central IdP policy for MCP

Skills over MCP. Community working group exploring rich structured instructions discovered through MCP (related to how this fleet already uses skill files). See https://modelcontextprotocol.io/community/working-groups/skills-over-mcp

lessons.title: 0008 . What's new in 2026-07-28
lessons.summary:
Treat this as a migration brief. Teams still coding against initialize handshakes and session headers will fail compatibility checks against the July 2026 revision.

Migration mindset. Call initialize, wait for initialized: Put version + capabilities on every request; optional server/discover Stick to Mcp-Session-Id: Explicit state handles in tool args Server fires elicitation/create as its own request: Return input_required; client retries Core tasks/* blocking result: Opt into Tasks extension; poll Subscribe via resources subscribe / HTTP GET: subscriptions/listen

Feature lifecycle. Active → Deprecated (≥12 months) → Removed. Registry: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/deprecated

lessons.title: 0009 . Security and trust
lessons.summary:
The protocol cannot enforce ethics. Hosts must. Users need to see what data leaves the machine and which tools run before they run.

Spec principles. User consent and control — explicit authorization; clear UI Data privacy — host consent before exposing user data to servers; no silent retransmit Tool safety — tools are arbitrary code execution; annotations are untrusted unless the server is trusted; consent before invoke

Auth highlights (2026-07-28). Prefer OAuth for remote user data Validate iss when present (RFC 9207) Prefer Client ID Metadata Documents over Dynamic Client Registration Bind credentials to the issuing authorization server; do not reuse across issuers Protect MRTR requestState if it influences authorization

Fleet standing rules. Never commit API keys, OAuth client secrets, cookies, or service-account JSON Prefer local stdio for high-sensitivity local tools (calendar, drawio) Do not point Draw.io at the hosted MCP App Server URL Redact sensitive prompts before cloud enhancement layers (e.g. Skywork)

lessons.title: 0010 . Fleet MCP map
lessons.summary:
On snapdragon-grok, MCP is how Grok reaches Exa, Firecrawl, Google Calendar, Playwright, Tasks, Perplexity, and (when healthy) Draw.io and Runway. Skills still teach workflows; MCP attaches live tools.

Skills vs MCP (keep the split). Skill: Markdown playbook the agent loads MCP server: Live tool/resource endpoint Hermes CLI: Terminal wrapper around APIs (often no MCP)

Grok MCP (lean set, 2026-09-07). From workspace Agents.md / live session: exa: on firecrawl: on google-calendar: on playwright: on

Host keeps conversation history; servers stay isolated

A.name: Protocol core
A.100: Map the actors. Host vs Client vs Server; tools / resources / prompts; JSON-RPC; stdio vs Streamable HTTP at altitude.
A.200: Speak the RPCs. server/discover, */list, tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get, subscriptions/listen; _meta fields; resultType; caching (ttlMs, cacheScope).
A.300: Design for isolation. Progressive tool discovery across many servers; capability negotiation; when a server must not see peer context; error-code ranges.

B.name: 2026-07-28 changes
B.100: Name the breaks. No sessions / no initialize; MRTR replaces server-initiated requests; Tasks left core; Roots/Sampling/Logging deprecated.
B.200: Trace each replacement. _meta on every request; InputRequiredResult + retry; subscriptions/listen; Tasks extension; Streamable HTTP without Last-Event-ID resume.
B.300: Migrate under ambiguity. Dual-stack hosts during SDK lag; detecting protocol era; SEP trail; feature lifecycle Active → Deprecated (≥12 months) → Removed.

C.name: Security & authorization
C.100: Consent principles. User control, data privacy, tool safety; treat annotations as untrusted.
C.200: Auth mechanics. OAuth for remote user data; validate iss; Client ID Metadata Documents vs DCR; requestState integrity (HMAC/AEAD).
C.300: Threat models. Confused-deputy / tool poisoning; local-install risks (SEP-1024); enterprise-managed auth extension; policy for stdio vs remote.

D.name: Build & labs
D.100: Inventory. Map your host config servers to transport + trust tier.
D.200: Inspector + one server. Discover → list → call; note ttlMs; compare a local stdio server vs a remote HTTP server.
D.300: Migration brief. Capstone: what breaks if a dependency still speaks 2025-11-25; Skills vs MCP vs CLI decision for one workflow.
